mentions.name: Studio Galois
mentions.description: A line of math, science, and CS-inspired jewelry whose pieces are beautiful but carry hidden scientific meaning. Two styles so far: lambda calculus based pieces (a y-combinator earring and an expression that computes Graham's number) and quantum computing circuit pieces, sold online with lengthy science explanations of what each design represents.
mentions.problem: Marketing and selling the jewelry is the hardest part; their pieces were previously carried by a jewelry store whose owner retired.
mentions.source_excerpt:
My wife and I are working on a math/science/CS-inspired jewelry: pieces that are beautiful but have a (maybe a little hidden) meaning. E.g. earrings that are actually the y-combinator from lambda calculus.

We have two styles as of now: lambda calculus based pieces (the y-combinator, and an expression that computes Graham's number), and quantum computing circuits.
mentions.author: alphaBetaGamma

mentions.name: Studio Galois
mentions.description: This project designs and sells math, science, and CS-inspired jewelry whose pieces stand on their own aesthetically while carrying hidden meaning. One style is lambda-calculus based (depicting the Tromp diagram), including Y-combinator earrings and a pendant depicting a lambda expression computing Graham's number; the other is quantum-computing circuits based on the author's physics-professor brother's research, such as a pendant that is a non-local controlled-NOT gate. Production uses a custom DSL the author wrote to describe the pieces, with an interpreter that produces CAD files, then 3D printing or lost-wax casting. Pieces are on consignment in a jewelry store, with museum-store placement in progress.
